races.notes: No candidate reached 50%+1 in the Aug 18 primary (Moore 9,023 / 29.25%; Haley 8,831 / 28.63%; Koch 8,577 / 27.81%; Manley 4,413 / 14.31%). The top two, Moore and Haley, meet on the Nov 3 ballot. Names shown as printed on the Aug 18 ballot; SOE finance records list them as Christopher Moore and Dr. John L. Haley.

candidates.name: Chris Moore
candidates.background: Incumbent (joined the board Nov 2022); retired U.S. Navy captain; senior program manager at General Dynamics IT (per SOE candidate statement).
platform: Running for re-election to continue what he describes as recent gains for students and the district, and says more work is needed to build on them.
Says every decision and every dollar spent should be judged by the question "How does this benefit the student?"
Wants sustained improvement in results for all students and for the teachers and administrators who support them.
Emphasizes the board's budget and policy roles and says his contract and budget management experience helps him oversee the district's budget.
candidates.platform_note: No campaign website found; platform from the candidate statement filed with the SOE.

candidates.name: John Haley
candidates.background: 30+ years with Bay District Schools, including principal of J.R. Arnold High and district Executive Director of Operations (per campaign site).
platform: Says board decisions should start with whether they benefit students ("Students First, Politics Last").
Wants to modernize school facilities to expand career and technical programs that let students earn credentials for high-demand careers while still in school.
Wants teachers and support staff to have the resources they need and fair pay, and wants their feedback considered in decisions.
Supports strong school security, school resource officers, practiced emergency protocols and action on bullying.
Says classroom technology should support teachers, not replace them.
Pledges fiscal responsibility and a stronger connection between the District Office and local schools.

candidates.name: Colleen Koch
candidates.background: Bay District Schools classroom teacher; certified teacher since 2003 (per SOE candidate statement).
platform: Says "our children are not a business" and that education is a lifelong endeavor.
Wants technology in the classroom used responsibly.
Wants classroom teachers to get the support they need.
Says she would advocate for students, families and educators and help the board make sound decisions that affect parents and staff.
candidates.platform_note: No campaign website found; platform from the candidate statement filed with the SOE.

races.notes: City election held with the Nov 3, 2026 general election. Ward is a residency requirement; voting is citywide.

candidates.name: Bobby J. Birdsell
candidates.background: Incumbent Ward I commissioner; security professional, retired U.S. Air Force senior NCO and paramedic (per SOE candidate statement).
platform: Points to his current work on Callaway policy decisions, budget oversight and long-term planning.
Says his military, security and paramedic experience taught him that preparation and teamwork matter in decisions.
candidates.platform_note: No campaign website found; SOE candidate statement is mostly biographical and lists no specific policy proposals.

candidates.name: Karen Custer
candidates.background: Chemical engineer (process and safety engineering); co-founded a general contracting business (per SOE candidate statement).
platform: Wants to end fees for public records requests by Callaway residents, require city-owned phones for official business and make city emails searchable.
Wants to restore decorum in commission meetings with clear time limits so residents can speak without interruption.

Supports updating land development codes (setbacks, driveway space, street widths for emergency vehicles) and a temporary moratorium on incompatible residential development until those standards are in place.
Wants close review of traffic impacts from new development, especially along Highway 22.
Wants advance approval for any spending over budget, closer oversight of contracts and budgets, and to explore an independent review of city finances.

races.office: City of Panama City Beach Council, Ward 1
races.notes: Open seat; the city website lists Paul Casto as Ward 1 council member and he is not a candidate. Council members are elected citywide. Scott Heilmann filed but did not qualify.

candidates.name: Carlos Sanchez
candidates.background: Retired U.S. Air Force Chief Master Sergeant (EOD); utilities operations manager (per campaign site).
platform: Wants more security and law enforcement presence on the east end of the beach, building on the 2026 Spring Break approach.
Wants to prioritize disaster resilience, with infrastructure built to withstand storms and well-tested emergency procedures.
Wants to upgrade underground utilities, use cost-saving technology such as advanced water metering, and keep wastewater systems environmentally sound.
Wants to streamline city services, cut waste and publish data-driven performance measures (KPIs) so residents can see how tax dollars are used.
Wants better communication with residents about city operations, projects and decisions.
Wants growth balanced with residents' needs, including easing traffic congestion.

candidates.name: Grant Wittstruck
candidates.background: Local small business owner; has served on the PCB Planning Board and the city Half-Cent Sales Tax Oversight Committee (per SOE candidate statement).
platform: Proposes a Homestead Assessment Discount Program to lower city fire and stormwater assessments for homesteaded residents.
Wants free spectator access to the Russell-Fields City Pier for residents, with possible changes to visitor fees to cover the cost.
Wants to support police, fire, EMS and lifeguards, continue the current Spring Break approach and strengthen emergency preparedness.
Wants roads, water, sewer and stormwater systems to keep pace with growth, with new development paying its fair share.
Wants to protect neighborhoods from excessive density, invest in parks and youth recreation, and improve sidewalks.
Supports an annual Tourism Local Investment and Impact Report on how tourism dollars benefit residents.

candidates.name: Scott Heilmann
candidates.background: Family nurse practitioner (per SOE candidate statement).
platform: Says he has pushed for fiscal responsibility and government transparency at council meetings.
Wants the city to follow its own rules and the laws it is responsible for upholding.
Wants balance between residents, communities and businesses so growth does not come at residents' expense.
Says he is running to provide independent leadership for residents.
candidates.platform_note: Filed but did not qualify; platform from the candidate statement filed with the SOE.

Wants to listen to residents, support local businesses and push for common-sense planning.

races.office: City of Lynn Haven Mayor (partial term)
races.notes: A recall election for Mayor Jesse Nelson was set for Jan 20, 2026, with Dave Lowery as the only qualified candidate to fill the seat. Nelson resigned before the vote and the SOE canceled the recall election, so no votes were cast. The City Commission then unanimously appointed Lowery to serve until the next regular election (April 20, 2027). The SOE has no results for this contest; the outcome is from local news reports.

candidates.name: Dave Lowery
candidates.background: Retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel; college professor of public administration (per SOE candidate statement).
platform: Says he is not seeking office to advance a political agenda.
Wants to support city staff and respect the role of the Lynn Haven City Commission.
Wants to keep city operations professional.
Wants to protect Lynn Haven taxpayers while stabilizing the city budget.
Wants to restore public trust in local government.
candidates.platform_note: Platform from the candidate statement filed with the SOE for the canceled Jan 20, 2026 recall election.

The Nov 3 sample ballot is only available as a personalized request form on bayvotesfl.gov. The active race list was assembled from the SOE 'Offices up for Election' page, SOE/VoterFocus candidate statuses, the Notice of General Election (county and special district offices) and the SOE snapshot sheets for Callaway and Panama City Beach, which list Nov 3, 2026 as their election date.

Incumbents not confirmed: Lake Powell CDD Seat 2; Springfield Wards 3 and 4; Mexico Beach Groups 4 and 5. Timothy Campbell's incumbency (County Judge G1) relies on a court-directory link that could not be opened.
Mexico Beach Groups 4 and 5: exact close of qualifying not confirmed (2026 snapshot no longer posted); decided_date left null.

Lynn Haven mayor (partial term): no SOE result exists because the Jan 20, 2026 recall election was canceled. Outcome (appointment of Dave Lowery) and date are from WJHG/WMBB reports; decided_date 2026-01-13 is the Tuesday commission meeting those reports describe.

Out of scope and not included: Circuit Judge, 14th Circuit Groups 7 and 10 (multi-county), and all state and federal races. Lynn Haven's five charter amendments on the Aug 18 ballot are ballot measures, not candidate races. No mosquito-control or soil and water district seats are on Bay County's 2026 ballot according to the SOE offices list. Panama City, Parker and other Lynn Haven/Mexico Beach seats are up in April 2027, not 2026.

Candidate names follow printed 2026 ballots where available (Aug 18 primary, Apr 21 Springfield); for Nov 3 city and CDD races and races decided at qualifying, names follow SOE candidate filings because the full Nov 3 ballot text was not available.
Candidate status values 'lost', 'did_not_qualify' and 'appointed' were added beyond the original enum to describe these cases accurately (see status_legend).
